issues.problem: English: '1 extrema' uses plural for singular
English: '1 inflection points' uses plural for singular

issues.where: sign beat and inflection beat, all presets, both locales
issues.problem: Uses approximation symbol '≈' for exact values (e.g., 'x₀ ≈ -1', 'x ≈ 0', 'x ≈ 1', 'x ≈ 2')
issues.fix: Change '≈' to '=' since all critical points and inflection points are exact

factErrors: Frames cubic/index 6, pure-cubic/index 5 and neg-cubic/index 6: the unqualified assertion that an inflection point is never an extremum is false without the polynomial-scope restriction. For example, the function defined by f(x)=x² for x<0, f(0)=0 and f(x)=√x for x>0 has both a local minimum and a concavity change at 0. The statement is true for the displayed cubics but must be scoped accordingly.

Beat sketch and the opening claim in every preset: the marked extrema and inflection point are not enough special data to determine the graph by themselves. Roots or intercepts, end behavior and complete monotonicity/concavity intervals are missing; for example, x² and 2x² have the same sole marked minimum but different graphs.

issues.where: script preset pure-cubic between frames 2 and 4
issues.problem: Frame 3, which establishes that the double root of f′ does not cause a sign change, is never displayed or narrated; the script jumps directly to the claim that there are no extrema.
issues.fix: Insert frame 3 and explain explicitly that f′(x)=3x²>0 for x≠0 and f′(0)=0, so f is increasing through 0 without an extremum.

issues.where: script preset square after the extrema step
issues.problem: The lesson promises an inflection-point step and concludes that there are none, but it never computes f″ or justifies the conclusion.
issues.fix: Add a beat stating f″(x)=2>0 for every real x, so concavity never changes and there is no inflection point.

issues.where: roots and extrema steps in all presets
issues.problem: The walkthrough often gives only the number of roots or displays coordinates in vars/state without showing the equations and substitutions. Exact integer roots are also written with the unnecessary approximation sign.
issues.fix: Show the solving and substitution explicitly, for example 3x²−3=0 gives x=−1,1 and f(−1)=2, f(1)=−2; use x₀=xᵢ=... rather than ≈ for exact values.

issues.where: all frame-0 states and the prediction sequence
issues.problem: The complete polynomial curve is visible before the prediction questions, so its turns and hence the intended answers can already be inferred. The derivative is also already visible when the sign question is asked.
issues.fix: Begin with axes and only disclosed information, or mask the relevant parts of f and f′; reveal each curve, sign change and extremum only after the prediction.

issues.problem: No lesson step explicitly obtains the x-intercepts, y-intercept, end behavior or full monotonicity and concavity intervals, so students cannot carry out the stated drawing procedure reliably.
issues.fix: Add sign charts and end-behavior analysis. Include roots −√3,0,√3 for x³−3x and roots 0,3 for −x³+3x², together with the relevant concavity intervals.

issues.where: sign interaction in cubic and neg-cubic; pure-cubic interaction
issues.problem: The same generic positive-to-negative question is repeated even when the next critical point has a negative-to-positive transition. The pure-cubic path has no genuine prediction question.
issues.fix: Ask what will happen at each actual critical point before revealing its sign change, and ask the pure-cubic student to predict whether the stationary point at 0 is an extremum.

issues.problem: Saying that the tangent at an inflection point is usually not horizontal is a weak correction and is misleading in this lesson: at the origin, x³ has a horizontal tangent while still being an inflection point and not an extremum.
issues.fix: Define an inflection point solely by a change of concavity and explicitly note that a horizontal tangent does not rule out an inflection point.

issues.problem: The wording f′=0 is presented as the full general definition of a critical point, although the standard definition also includes points where f′ does not exist. It is valid for these polynomial presets because their derivatives exist everywhere.
issues.fix: State that, for these differentiable polynomials, critical points are exactly the roots of f′; optionally mention the other branch of the general definition when transferring to arbitrary functions.

issues.problem: The title promises all polynomials of degree at most 3, but the walkthrough covers only selected quadratics and cubics. The stated roots-of-f′ procedure does not address constant or linear polynomials, especially a constant function whose derivative is identically zero.
issues.fix: Either retitle the chapter as selected degree-2 and degree-3 examples or add separate linear and constant cases.

issues.where: English alt text in the square and done steps
issues.problem: There are agreement errors such as “There are 1 critical points,” “1 extrema” and “1 inflection points,” which reduce clarity even though the meaning matches the Vietnamese.
issues.fix: Use dynamic singular/plural forms: “There is 1 critical point,” “1 extremum” and “1 inflection point.”
